_note: 調味料の系譜。品目ハブ（/en/eat/seasoning/）の横並び表と、各系譜ページがここから描く。出典は docs/research/ferment-egg-2026-10-11.md と各系譜ページの sources。醤油・卵は published。酢・みりんはメモの A 項に素材があるが系譜ページ未執筆のため planned、era は「—」。味噌は nabe、だしは dashi、漬物・納豆は rice-sides の系譜で扱うのでここには行を作らない
name: Seasonings

origin.place: From Chinese jiang; Yuasa (Wakayama) by tradition, Noda and Choshi (Chiba) for dark soy

cells.made: Soybeans, wheat and salt; koji mash matured about 6–8 months in tanks, a year or more in barrels
cells.types: Dark koikuchi (84.9% of 2024 shipments), light usukuchi, tamari, saishikomi, white shiro
cells.use: Cooking and at the table; light soy where the colour of the food should show
cells.marker: Chiba ships 37.6%; many factories take visitors, mostly by booking

origin.era: Eaten from the early Edo period; raw-egg rules from 1999

cells.made: Washed, disinfected, inspected and packed at grading centres; 96% domestic
cells.types: Raw on rice, onsen tamago, rolled omelette (sweet atsuyaki in Kanto, dashimaki in Kansai)
cells.use: Best-before date is for eating raw, 21 days at most; cook thoroughly after it
cells.marker: 320 eggs a person in 2023, fourth in one international count

cells.made: Brewed vinegar (grain, black, fruit) or synthetic vinegar
cells.types: Rice vinegar; sake-lees vinegar (kasuzu) from the later Edo period
cells.use: Sake-lees vinegar spread with Edo-style sushi

cells.made: Steamed glutinous rice and rice koji in shochu, 40–60 days at 20–30 °C, then pressed
cells.use: Sweetness, shine, flavour soaking in, keeps food from falling apart, masks smells
cells.marker: Two origin stories; this site does not choose
